title: Best Crime Dramas in the World Right Now
intro: Crime drama is the genre that every culture keeps reinventing from first principles - the same bones, radically different flesh. This list crosses five languages and four continents to find the shows that understand something true about power, violence, and consequence, not just procedural mechanics.

picks.title: Breaking Bad
picks.one_line: The still-undefeated template for prestige crime television - a transformation story so precisely engineered that every rewatch reveals another layer of foreshadowing.

picks.title: True Detective: Season 1
picks.one_line: McConaughey and Harrelson in a Southern Gothic murder mystery that works as philosophy lecture and landscape film as much as crime procedural.

picks.title: Mindhunter
picks.one_line: David Fincher's FBI serial-killer procedural is less about the crimes than the men who convinced themselves they could think like monsters - and what that does to them.

picks.title: Ozark
picks.one_line: A money-launderer trapped in escalating cartel pressure in the Missouri Ozarks - slower than Breaking Bad, darker, and Julia Garner's Ruth Langmore is a series-defining supporting turn.

faq.q: Is Breaking Bad really still the best crime series ever made?
faq.a: By consensus, yes - and that consensus has held for over a decade against serious challengers. Better Call Saul (same universe, same showrunner) is arguably its equal in craft; watch Breaking Bad first regardless. If you want something that pushes the claim, True Detective Season 1 and Mindhunter are the most credible counterarguments.

faq.q: Is there a non-English pick here worth the subtitles?
faq.a: The Glory earns its place. The Korean revenge thriller built around school bullying turns patient and methodical rather than loud, and it sits comfortably next to Mindhunter and True Detective Season 1 as character-first crime writing. It is also the title here most viewers have not already worked through.
